title: Plantings by plan and in fact
description: Draw up a seasonal calendar that takes the location into account, and record the real dates and changes in conditions separately.

blocks.text: The gardener picks a location and crops, gets the suggested dates and records when they actually planted. The shift from the plan is kept separately, so that later it is clear why the events did not match the calendar.

quote.text: Don't trust the planting dates - the app lists many months as OK to plant for some veggies (ie: March-July) - but then when you click into the details, it may only be suitable for planting in May. Which dates do I trust?

blocks.text: From the seasonal plan to the real dates

It is better to start with a limited set of crops and checked local information. The general calendar and the detailed card have to use the same basis: months that contradict each other, as in the review, make a choice impossible.
Show the basis of the calculation

A seasonal plan calls for different work on content than a home watering journal. Without reliable starting dates, a handsome schedule creates unwarranted confidence; planning by hand with visible conditions is more honest than automation that has not been confirmed.
